source_text: So, geting rid of the while True seems really important.  Fixing the bell issues is something I can pass to another agent.  It's good that we should have a "retry" loop, especially if it takes 10-11 minutes to reach a fail, that needs to go into the background ... but then we need to "retry better" i.e. make improvements not loop forever on the the same fail.  I also am thinking that we might want to revisit the "fork Python" idea we discussed, i.e. if we can get 10 minutes in, make an incremental series of fixes against forks, we could increment forward.  The other option, which may be better, is to show me the curriculum that we're working against.  Otherwise I'm basically sending dispatches into a 6-minute void each time and have no sense of progress.

reply_text:
Bounded the retry loop; now adding a test that a rebuild which doesn't fix the lookup fails loudly instead of spinning.Loop fixed and committed. Now looking at the census so I can show you a concrete curriculum for the blank path.㊥ (summary) The `while True` loop is now bounded. A dispatch I've just sent produces a real curriculum for the blank path: every constant Lean runs for an empty file, and the port's status on each. You should see that table instead of the next stop. Job `invoke-…ddaddf17`, parked as `park-a945429c`, this time with the session field.

㊢ (the loop) The fix is in `/tmp/mfs-blank`: `5e44804` adds the test and `da42b39` makes the change. Each lookup may now rebuild a given declaration only once. If a declaration is still missing after its own rebuild, the run fails with an error naming it. The retry still moves forward through *different* declarations, and since there are finitely many, it can't run forever. The new test hung on codex-4's version (I killed it at 30 s) and passes now. All 3 blank-startup tests pass. It isn't on startup-linux yet; I'll land it there along with codex-4's two commits.

㊩ (what the existing curriculum covered) PLAN.md does have a curriculum, but it doesn't cover what you need now. Its Phase 1 and 2 maps compare *which syntax kinds exist* in Lean and in the port. Blank startup instead depends on *which code runs*, and nothing in the plan lists that. So each run has only shown us the next stop. The census has part of the answer: just 26 constants are recorded as executed after init for an empty file (`ParserFn.run`, `mkParserState`, `FileMap.ofString`, `Trie.find?`, extension `mkInitial`s and so on). That table only covers the 20,173 initializer-closure rows, though. It leaves out the parse loop itself, including `testParseModule`, where we're stopped now.

㊭ (what the new job produces) `BLANK-CURRICULUM.tsv` and `.md`:
1. Every constant Lean executes after init for `empty.lean`, from a fresh callgrind run, each with file:line.
2. A check that the port's entry point, `testParseModule`, does the same parse as `lean empty.lean`'s frontend, with any differences named.
3. For each constant, the macros and notations in its body that the port must expand to compile it (`term#[_,]` is one).
4. The port's status for each: compiled, failed with an error, or not reached, taken from evidence only.
5. Counts.

After that, each fix should move a number, such as "41 of 60 compiled". Where single-declaration probes are fast, a fix can also be checked in seconds rather than with an 11-minute run.

🈖 (the fork-Python idea) I'd put it after the curriculum. Forking at minute 10 only helps when a fix lands in code the parent process hasn't loaded yet. Our fixes are almost all in the compiler, which is already loaded and holding state by then. Two cheaper ways to shorten each attempt:
- Run warm. S2 brought an unchanged warm start down to 41 s, so cold runs can be kept for acceptance.
- Use the curriculum's per-declaration probes.

If runs are still slow after both, forking is worth a look then.

🈸 (bell issue, for the agent you pass it to) The spec in short: a park on an `emacs*` surface with no `session` is queued under `[agent ""]`, which the buffer never polls (`agent-repl-park.el:307`). Meanwhile `auto-bellback-suppressing-park` (`http.clj` ~1290) drops the bellback because "a park will wake the agent". The result is that the wake is lost with no signal. There are 17 stuck items for claude-4 in `/tmp/futon3c-parked-on.edn`. Fix either by rejecting such parks at POST, or by suppressing the bellback only after the ready item has been leased and acked. Then clear the stale queue.

CLAUDE.md's park template does include `session`; I dropped it. I've saved a memory so future parks include it.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (server guard) Shall I have the server refuse a park on an `emacs*` surface that has no session (a 400 at park time)? The other option is to have the bellback suppressed only when the wake is actually delivered. Either one turns this from a silent loss into a visible error. As far as I can tell, the 17 stuck items are all stale now and can be cleared.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (what codex-4 delivered at 15:57) Commits `891d7d1` (test) and `1a24607` (fix), in `/tmp/mfs-amb`, not pushed. Blank startup no longer compiles the whole import closure up front. Instead, when execution reaches a declaration that hasn't been generated yet, the port builds it then and retries. Codex-4 reports 55 gate tests passed. In the cold run, the only declaration demanded directly was `Lean.Parser.testParseModule`. The run stopped after 671 s at 4.35 GiB peak, with no OOM. The stop is an unsupported `term#[_,]` macro (array literal) in the body of `testParseModule`. Unlike `term[_]`, this one is on Lean's real empty-file path, because Lean calls `testParseModule` for an empty file.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (one thing from my diff read) The new retry in `generated_roundtrip_source_external_runtime.py` is a `while True:`. If a rebuild fails to supply the declaration and the same requirement is raised again, it loops forever and gives no error. I'll add a guard that fails loudly on a repeated requirement before landing it on startup-linux. Then I'll dispatch the `term#[_,]` stop and park with the session field.
